Olivia Nguyen: hey team — I'm on my first day and I can't access the internal docs site or ssh to the bastion after connecting to the VPN. `ssh bastion` times out. Any onboarding steps I missed?

Ashwin Rao: welcome! which VPN client did you use? Okta SSO -> tunnel agent? Also can you paste the output of `ip route` or `ifconfig` so we can see the routes?

Olivia Nguyen: using Okta VPN (TunnelAgent). After SSO it shows connected. Here's `ip route` output:
```
default via 192.0.2.1 dev en0
10.0.0.0/8 via 172.22.36.1 dev tun0
```
But accessing `internal.redwood.local` times out. curl to 10.0.1.12:443 fails.

Ashwin Rao: two quick things — 1) split-tunnel policy sometimes doesn't push the internal DNS search domain, so DNS for `internal.redwood.local` goes to public DNS; 2) check that your resolver has the corporate search domain. Run `scutil --dns` on mac or `systemd-resolve --status` on linux.

Olivia Nguyen: on mac, `scutil --dns` shows no search domain for our internal zone. Also ssh to bastion gives `ssh: connect to host bastion.redwood.internal port 22: Connection refused`.

Jordan Lee: @Olivia try hitting bastion by IP first: `ssh ubuntu@10.0.2.5` — if IP works but name fails it's DNS. If IP fails too, check security group / source CIDR. New hires sometimes need their Okta group added to the bastion SG.

Ashwin Rao: I checked the onboarding ticket — your Okta group (new-hires-nyc) wasn't in the bastion SG allowlist. I just added the rule. You might need to disconnect/reconnect the VPN for the new session to pick up the change.

infra-bot: Created ticket #INFRA-4721 and applied SG rule change. Rolling to bastion SG in us-east-1. ETA ~2 min.

Olivia Nguyen: reconnected VPN and `ssh ubuntu@10.0.2.5` works now! still can't resolve `internal.redwood.local` though.

Ashwin Rao: for DNS, try this on your laptop (mac):
```
# add corporate DNS server and search domain on mac
sudo networksetup -setdnsservers "Wi-Fi" 10.0.0.2
sudo networksetup -setsearchdomains "Wi-Fi" internal.redwood.local
# flush resolver
sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
```
I'll also push an update to the Okta VPN profile to include the search domain so future connections pick it up automatically.

Jordan Lee: FYI if you're on a corporate-managed laptop some EDR agents override DNS — if you're on personal, ping me and I'll add a host exception.

okta-bot: User Olivia Nguyen (olivia.nguyen@redwood.com) authenticated via Okta at 2025-11-15T14:13:02Z

Olivia Nguyen: after the DNS change `curl https://internal.redwood.local` returns HTML and the docs load. Thanks!

Ashwin Rao: sweet. Next steps: we'll add you to the permanent Okta group and update the onboarding checklist to remind new hires to re-establish VPN after SG updates. @maya can you add that to the runbook?

Jordan Lee: noted. tagging #new-hires checklist.

SRE Oncall: leaving a note — if anyone else on newer macOS sees DNS bleed through split-tunnel, try `sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder` after adding the search domain.

Olivia Nguyen: all good now. Thanks everyone :tada:
